==English==
{{wp}}
{{wikidata lexeme|L5512}}

===Alternative forms===
* {{alt|en|imployer||obsolete}}

===Etymology===
From {{suf|en|employ|er|id2=agent noun}}, {{etydate|late 16th century|nocap=1}}.{{ref|{{R:OED Online|pos=n}}}} Compare {{cog|fr|employeur}}.

===Pronunciation===
* {{IPA|en|/ɪmˈplɔɪə/|/ɛmˈplɔɪə/|a=RP}}
** {{audio|en|LL-Q1860 (eng)-Vealhurl-employer.wav|a=Southern England}}
* {{enPR|ĭm-ploiʹər|ĕm-ploiʹər|a=GA,CA}}, {{IPA|en|/ɪmˈplɔɪ.ɚ/|/ɛmˈplɔɪ.ɚ/}}
* {{IPA|en|/ɪmˈploɪə/|/emˈploɪə/|a=Australia}}
* {{IPA|en|/əmˈploɪə/|/emˈploɪə/|a=NZ}}
* {{rhymes|en|ɔɪ.ə(ɹ)|s=3}}
* {{hyph|en|em|ploy|er}}

===Noun===
{{en-noun}}

# {{senseid|en|Q3053337}} A [[person]], [[firm]] or other [[entity]] which pays for or hires the services of another person.
#: {{ant|en|employee}}
#* {{RQ:Churchill Celebrity|chapter=10|passage=The skipper Mr. Cooke had hired at Far Harbor was a God-fearing man with a luke warm interest in his new billet and '''employer''', and had only been prevailed upon to take charge of the yacht after the offer of an emolument equal to half a year's sea pay of an ensign in the navy.}}
#* {{quote-book
|en
|year=1913
|first=James Harrington
|last=Boyd
|chapter=Distinctions Between the Common Law, Employer's Liability Laws, Workmen's Industrial Insurance Laws, and Workmen's Compensation Laws as Remedies for Compensating Workmen Injured in the Due Course of their Employment
|title=Workmen's Compensation and Industrial Insurance under Modern Conditions
|volume=I
|volumeurl=https://archive.org/details/workmenscompensa01boyd/
|location=Indianapolis
|publisher=w:Bobbs-Merrill Company
|OCLC=4590626
|page=1
|pageurl=https://archive.org/details/workmenscompensa01boyd/page/1/
|text=Today, at common law, the '''employer's''' duty to his employé is to use ordinary and reasonable care for the safety of his employé while he is performing his work.}}
